questions.q: What does the Sharpe ratio measure?
options: Excess return divided by total risk (standard deviation)
Total return divided by the number of holdings
Excess return divided by tracking error against a benchmark
questions.explain: Sharpe ratio = (Rp - Rf) / sigma_p, measuring reward per unit of total risk, including both systematic and unsystematic components.

questions.q: When is the Treynor ratio the more appropriate metric than the Sharpe ratio?
options: When evaluating a portfolio that is one piece of a larger, already well-diversified holding, where only systematic risk (beta) matters
When the portfolio has no risk-free rate available
When comparing two completely unrelated asset classes
The Treynor ratio is never more appropriate than the Sharpe ratio
questions.explain: Treynor divides by beta rather than total risk, which is the right choice when unsystematic risk will be diversified away at a higher portfolio level, so only systematic risk contribution is relevant.

The portfolio's actual return minus the return CAPM would have predicted given its beta — a direct measure of risk-adjusted outperformance
The correlation between the portfolio and the risk-free asset
The number of factors used to construct the portfolio
questions.explain: Jensen's alpha = Rp - [Rf + beta_p*(Rm - Rf)]. A positive alpha means the portfolio outperformed what its systematic risk exposure alone would justify under CAPM.

What is the difference between the allocation effect and the selection effect in performance attribution?
options: They are the same thing measured in different units

Allocation effect comes from over/underweighting sectors or asset classes vs. a benchmark; selection effect comes from which specific securities were picked within a given sector, holding its weight fixed
Allocation effect only applies to bonds, and selection effect only applies to stocks
Selection effect measures total portfolio risk, while allocation effect measures total portfolio return
questions.explain: Allocation effect isolates the impact of the top-down sector/asset-class weighting decision, while selection effect isolates the impact of the bottom-up security-picking decision within each sector — separating these clarifies which decision actually drove a manager's performance.
